messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — canary pool shows steady memory growth over ~6h after today's kernel-router + kv-warmup change merged this morning. Not hitting OOM yet but longctx allocation ramps for seqlen-heavy requests. /cc @marta @vikram

marta: saw same on 3 canary nodes. pmap snapshot attached, heaplet rss ~+22% vs baseline. low churn but fragmentation creeping. quick grep of alloc traces shows warmup path allocations spiking.

vikram: FYI nightly CI flagged this too: `load/kv_mem` regressed. CI link: https://ci.internal/reports/4821 (regressed +18%, threshold 5%). Suspect PR 3862 that landed kernel-router prefetch + warmup changes.

ci-bot: build #4821: test load/kv_mem — REGRESSION +18% RSS (threshold 5%). Suspected commits: PR 3862 (kernel-router:prefetch + kv-warmup).

ashwin: quick pprof dump from one of the canaries:
```
(pprof) top10
  34.2MB  34.2MB  kv_cache::warm_start
  18.7MB  18.7MB  kernel_router::prefetch_chunk
  12.1MB  12.1MB  slab_allocator::alloc_page
```
Not definitive but points to warm_start path allocating more small objects -> fragmentation.

sam: can we reproduce locally with a small harness? I have a repro script: `tools/load_kv.py --seqlen 2048 --warmup 100 --concurrency 8`. That hits the growth in ~4 minutes.

marta: started `git bisect` across the last 24 commits touching the router + kv modules. Early sign: frag spike appears when warmup prefetch window increases from 8->16. seqlen sensitivity: only reproducible when seqlen >= 1536.

vikram: note: if we set `kv_warmup_prefetch=0` the memory slope disappears. So it's likely interaction between prefetch and slab hot-slab scattering. Could be the new prefetch path bypassing compact coalescer.

ashwin: rolling canary paused. ops: please halt further canary promotion — this is a rollout blocker until we triage.

ops: canary rollout paused, affected hosts quarantined. Created internal incident and pinned the canary group.

revert-bot: Created revert PR #3890 reverting PR 3862 (kernel-router warmup prefetch changes). Link: https://scm.internal/pull/3890

marta: applied revert to one canary subset; after revert the memory curves flatten — nodes look back to baseline in ~10 minutes. Confirming across replicated runs.

vikram: next steps: 1) collect full object maps with `jemalloc_stats` + `pprof` on repro; 2) run synthetic across seqlen sweep (512, 1024, 1536, 2048); 3) test toggling `kv_compact_coalesce` flag. Also consider adding a targeted unit test for warm_start path to catch fragmentation.

ashwin: thanks all. Marking this as rollout-blocker and opening a follow-up ticket to investigate a safe re-intent (smaller prefetch window + coalescer fix). If revert PR merges cleanly we'll proceed with canary rollback. :lock:

ci-bot: Revert PR #3890 merged to canary branch. Canary rollback in progress.
